topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, introduces the subject of complement, and frames its complexity and place within the course.

topics.label: Overview and Core Principles of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture, naming conventions, and central biochemical importance of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three distinct recognition pathways that converge to trigger C3 activation on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream processes through which activated complement directly destroys pathogens and stimulates immune action.

topics.label: Regulation of Complement and Host Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the distinct disease vulnerabilities and clinical presentations associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the evolutionary mechanisms pathogens deploy to subvert complement attack and their practical applications in biotechnology.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
